algorithms.title: Binary Heap & d-ary Heap Foundations & Operations
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(1) Peek, O(log N) Push/Pop, O(N) BuildHeap
algorithms.summary: Complete tree-based Priority Queue implementations (Min/Max Binary Heap and d-ary Heap) supporting O(1) peek, O(log N) push/pop, and linear O(N) buildHeap.
explanation: Binary Heap: Complete binary tree stored as contiguous array. Parent at `(i-1)//2`, children at `2*i + 1` and `2*i + 2`.
d-ary Heap: Each node has d children (at `d*i + 1` through `d*i + d`), reducing tree height to O(log_d N) for faster bubble-up operations.
Insert (Push): Append item at end, call `bubble_up` (sift-up) to restore heap property.
Extract (Pop): Swap root with last element, remove last element, call `sink_down` (sift-down) on root.
Build Heap (Floyd's Algorithm): Call `sink_down` on all non-leaf nodes from index `N//2 - 1` down to 0 in optimal linear O(N) time.

traceSteps: Push 5: Heap = [5, 10] (5 sifted up to root)
Push 2: Heap = [2, 5, 20, 10] (2 sifted up to root)
Pop(): Min root 2 extracted. 10 moved to root, sifted down -> Heap = [5, 10, 20].

algorithms.title: Top K Elements: K Largest & K Smallest
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(K) for Heap of size K
algorithms.summary: Finds the K largest (or K smallest) elements in an array using a Min-Heap (or Max-Heap) of bounded size K in O(N log K) time.
explanation: K Largest Pattern: Maintain a Min-Heap of size K.
Iterate through N array elements.
Push element into Min-Heap. If heap size exceeds K, pop the smallest element (`heappop()`).
After inspecting all N elements, the Min-Heap contains exactly the K largest elements!
K Smallest Pattern: Maintain a Max-Heap of size K using the same logic.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Extracts top K extreme values without sorting the entire array.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding K largest/smallest elements where N is large and K << N.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Search engine top search results, leaderboard rankings, streaming top K metrics.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Reduces O(N log N) sorting to O(N log K) time and O(K) space.

algorithms.title: Top K Frequent & K Closest Elements
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(N) for Frequency Map + O(K) for Heap
algorithms.summary: Solves Top K Frequent Elements and K Closest Points using HashMap frequency count combined with a Min-Heap of size K.
explanation: Top K Frequent: Build frequency count map `freq[x]`.
Maintain a Min-Heap storing pairs `(freq[x], x)` bounded to size K.
Pop when heap size exceeds K. The surviving elements are the K most frequent items.
K Closest Points to Origin: Store points in Max-Heap ordered by distance `x² + y²`. Maintain size K.

algorithms.title: Two Heaps Pattern: Stream Median & Sliding Median
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(log N) Insert, O(1) Find Median
algorithms.summary: Maintains dynamic median of incoming data stream or sliding window using Max-Heap for lower half and Min-Heap for upper half.
explanation: Maintain two heaps: `max_heap` for smaller half of numbers, `min_heap` for larger half of numbers.
Add Num: Push into `max_heap`. Move top of `max_heap` to `min_heap` to preserve value ordering.
Balance Heaps: If `len(min_heap) > len(max_heap)`, move top of `min_heap` back to `max_heap`.
Invariant: `max_heap` has size equal to or 1 greater than `min_heap`.
Find Median: If total numbers is odd, return `max_heap.top()`. If even, return `(max_heap.top() + min_heap.top()) / 2.0` in O(1) time.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes exact median of dynamic data streams in O(1) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When elements are continuously inserted or sliding in a window and instant median query is needed.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Financial real-time tick data analytics, signal noise filtering, SLA percentile calculators.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Provides instant O(1) median lookup with O(log N) insertion overhead.

algorithms.title: Heap Scheduling: Task Scheduler, CPU & Meeting Rooms II
algorithms.summary: Schedules CPU tasks and reserves meeting rooms using Priority Queue to track earliest ending resources and cooldown queues.
explanation: Meeting Rooms II: Sort intervals by start time. Maintain Min-Heap of end times of active meetings.
If `min_heap.top() <= start_time`: Re-use room! Pop old end time.
Push current meeting's end time. Size of Min-Heap = minimum conference rooms required.
Task Scheduler: Max-Heap of task frequencies + Cooldown Queue tracking `(available_time, task_freq)` to respect cooldown N.

traceSteps: Meeting [0, 30]: Push end time 30 -> Heap = [30]. Rooms = 1.
Meeting [5, 10]: start 5 < 30 (cannot reuse!). Push 10 -> Heap = [10, 30]. Rooms = 2.
Meeting [15, 20]: start 15 >= 10 (reuse room!). Pop 10, Push 20 -> Heap = [20, 30].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Schedules tasks or resource allocations under time/cooldown constraints.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When scheduling tasks, allocation of rooms/servers, or managing CPU execution order.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Operating system process schedulers, AWS EC2 instance reservation, calendar booking systems.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Min-heap tracks earliest available resource in O(log N) time per task.

algorithms.title: K-Way Merge: Merge K Sorted Arrays & Lists
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N log K) where N is total elements across K arrays
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(K) for Min-Heap of size K
algorithms.summary: Merges K sorted arrays or linked lists into a single sorted list using a Min-Heap of size K in O(N log K) time.
explanation: Initialize a Min-Heap of size K.
Push the first element of each of the K sorted arrays into the Min-Heap along with `(val, array_index, element_index)`.
Pop the smallest element from the heap and append to the output array.
If the popped element's array has more elements, push its next element `(arr[arr_idx][elem_idx + 1], arr_idx, elem_idx + 1)` into the heap.
Repeat until heap is empty.

traceSteps: Push first element of each array: MinHeap = [(1,A0), (2,A1), (3,A2)].
Continue until all K arrays are merged -> Output = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Combines K sorted input streams into one sorted output sequence.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When merging multiple sorted arrays, files, or linked lists.
wAnswers.whereUsed: External sorting of multi-gigabyte log files, database index merge joins.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Min-heap maintains log-time O(log K) selection per element across K streams.
